source: ESG Disclosure Guide Book (EDGB), the 'S' (Social) ESG-metric indicators (S-01–S-09) in the `standards` corpus, which map bank social disclosures to GRI topic codes GRI 401 / 403 / 404 / 405 / 406 / 412. As with the environmental checklist, the EDGB is the in-corpus anchor for which social GRI topics are material to banks; the GRI social topic-standard PDFs themselves are not in the knowledge base, so the standard GRI disclosure sub-codes are used. Scoped to high-materiality workforce, occupational-health-and-safety, diversity, and human-rights items. EDGB social indicators carried without a GRI topic code — S-04 (number of temporary employees), S-07 (count of human-rights violations), and S-10 (child/forced-labor policy, tagged WFE only) — are omitted because they fall outside a GRI-coded checklist. EDGB tags its human-rights-policy indicator (S-09) as a bare 'GRI 412'; it is mapped here to GRI 412-1 (human rights review / due diligence) as the closest standard GRI disclosure. Anti-corruption (GRI 205) and economic items (GRI 201/210/215) that the EDGB also carries are governance/economic, not social, and belong to the governance checklist.

items.description: New employee hires and employee turnover: the rates of new employee hires and of employee turnover during the reporting period, including where reported the split between voluntary and involuntary turnover, indicating workforce stability and retention.

Work-related injuries: the number and rate of work-related injuries and accidents (including fatalities and high-consequence injuries) arising from the bank's operations, reflecting occupational health and safety performance.
Average hours of training per employee: the average hours of training undertaken per employee during the reporting period, indicating the bank's investment in employee skills and development.

Diversity of employees: the composition of the bank's workforce (and, where reported, its governance bodies) broken down by gender and by age group across job levels, indicating diversity and equal opportunity.

Incidents of discrimination and non-discrimination measures: incidents of discrimination during the reporting period and any corrective actions taken, and/or the bank's non-discrimination and anti-sexual-harassment policy.
Human rights policy and due diligence: whether the bank has a formal human rights policy commitment and conducts human rights reviews or impact assessments across its operations and value chain.
